_readme: THE SHELF — the forty looks a church finds on a fresh install (wave 5, Track A).
ONE FILE, TWO READERS. `db/templates.rs` include_str!s this and seeds it BY NAME (never by id,
so a church's channel foreign keys are never repointed); `src/lib/shelf.test.js` reads the same
bytes and renders every entry through the real TemplateRender. The last time a shipped design
lived in two places they drifted by one row and a kiosk rendered a song through a scripture look.
EIGHT ROLES, FIVE EACH: Scripture, Song, Media, Announcement, Timer, Scrolling Lower Third,
SuperSource, Stage. Every entry is LAYER model — the region model stopped shipping in this wave,
which is what closes RG-140 and RG-141 at the source rather than by repairing the region fitter.
EVERY ENTRY DECLARES `layout.shows` EXPLICITLY, and every one declares all five kinds. That is
not a shrug: `layout.shows` is a per-SCREEN filter read at `Output.svelte` BEFORE
`resolveOutputTemplate`, so a narrow list on a screen's own template makes that screen silently
drop every other kind. What a template is FOR is the content-look register, not this list.
EVERY ENTRY CLEARS 7:1 BODY-TEXT CONTRAST against its own ground — the accessibility family
became the accessibility standard. `shelfcontrast.test.js` walks all forty with the same helper
`legibility.test.js` uses. A translucent band is held to its declared plate colour at FULL alpha,
and a scrim over a picture likewise: Relay cannot know what a camera or a photograph looks like,
and a contrast figure that pretended otherwise would be a number that lies (rule 18).
NO ENTRY WEARS A LAW COLOUR on a band or a ground: not amber (ON AIR), not amethyst (rehearsal),
not cyan (a guess). DECISIONS §21, CLAUDE.md rule 18.
`seed_key` IS THE IDENTITY THE LEGACY CONVERSION CANNOT DESTROY. RG-142 measured the previous,
byte-matching retirement at 0 of 21 against a real database, because `upgradeLegacyToLayers` had
already rewritten every row on mount. A seeded row now carries a stable slug that no conversion
touches, and `templates.edited_at` records that a human saved it.
`_design` is a note to a reader, not data. Nothing reads it.

templates.name: Scripture · Dayspring
templates._design: Warm ivory serif on deep charcoal; the reference beneath, small, tracked and right-aligned.

templates.name: Scripture · Meridian
templates._design: White display sans on pure black, centred. The 21:1 maximum.

templates.name: Scripture · Vellum
templates._design: Dark ink on a cream ground — the one light-ground scripture look, for a daylight room.

templates.name: Scripture · Indigo
templates._design: White sans on deep indigo; the reference in the SAME white, not a tint, so both clear the floor. A gradient ground was drawn in the design and is a flat colour here — a gradient cannot be measured, and an unmeasurable ground is not a pass.

templates.name: Scripture · Column
templates._design: Left-aligned under a hairline rule; the reference ABOVE the verse, not below.

templates.name: Song · Anthem
templates._design: Large centred display sans, white on black.

templates.name: Song · Chorus
templates._design: Ivory on deep plum, generous leading.

templates.name: Song · Open
templates._design: White on dark teal, a wide measure, the lightest look that still clears the floor.

templates.name: Song · Plain
templates._design: Pure black, the tightest margins and the largest type in the set.

templates.name: Song · Ember
templates._design: Warm white serif on a near-black brown.

templates.name: Media · Full
templates._design: The picture fills the frame. Nothing else — and so there is no body text to measure. The black ground under it is what keeps the look UNKEYED: `isKeyedTemplate` asks whether anything paints the whole frame, and a full-screen media slide that answered yes would be exempted from an opaque override by the transparency law and would refuse a blackout.

templates.name: Media · Caption
templates._design: Picture full-frame, one caption line on a solid plate at the foot. The caption is measured against its plate, never against the picture.

templates.name: Media · Frame
templates._design: Picture inset on a ground plate with a hairline mat.

templates.name: Media · Split
templates._design: Picture one half, words the other. The design drew the words as a `region`; a region layer is a COMPOSITE and `templateKind` reads it as SuperSource, which would file a Media row under the SuperSource rail. The words are a text layer instead, and the split is the same.

templates.name: Media · Wash
templates._design: Picture full-frame under a scrim so type over it stays legible. Measured against the scrim's own plate colour at full alpha — Relay cannot know what the picture behind it looks like.

templates.name: Announce · Board
templates._design: Title over body, left aligned, strong hierarchy.

templates.name: Announce · Card
templates._design: A centred card on a ground, generously padded.

templates.name: Announce · Bold
templates._design: One line, as large as the frame allows.

templates.name: Announce · List
templates._design: Title over stacked lines.

templates.name: Announce · Contrast
templates._design: White on black, the 21:1 maximum.

templates.name: Timer · Monolith
templates._design: Digits alone, full frame. No label layer at all — this is the one the dock fires at, and a label nobody typed is a word nobody can remove.

templates.name: Timer · Rail
templates._design: Digits with the clock beneath.

templates.name: Scroll · Banner
templates._design: A solid band with one crawling line.

templates.name: Scroll · Ribbon
templates._design: A thin band with a fixed label chip at the left and the crawl running beside it. The chip is a SIBLING painted after the crawl, not a second band member, and both halves of that are load-bearing: `bandLayout` stacks members vertically, so a second member is a second LINE (which hung 2% off the bottom of a band this thin), and it also overrides a member's x to the band's own inset, so a member can never sit beside another. An opaque chip over the left end of the crawl track is how a ticker does this.

templates.name: Scroll · Glass
templates._design: A translucent band at a declared alpha. The alpha is bounded so the PLATE still clears the floor at the value it ships with — the camera behind it is not part of the measurement, and a number that pretended otherwise would be a number that lies.

templates.name: Scroll · Bold
templates._design: A tall band and large type, for a room that reads from the back.

templates.name: Scroll · Clear
templates._design: Transparent ground, band only. Keys cleanly for OBS and for an ATEM fed over HDMI.

templates.name: Source · Word right
templates._design: Camera left, words right.

templates.name: Source · Word left
templates._design: Words left, camera right.

templates.name: Source · Tall
templates._design: Camera above, words below.

templates.name: Source · Inset
templates._design: A small camera inset beside a word slide — the keyed column is where the switcher puts the picture.

templates.name: Source · Even
templates._design: Equal halves.

templates.name: Stage · Reading
templates._design: The reading takes what is left; the clock beneath it.
